newsitem.title: JAPAN: M'bishi affiliate strikes oil in Papua New Guinea.
newsitem.headline: M'bishi affiliate strikes oil in Papua New Guinea.

text.p: Mitsubishi Oil Co Ltd said on Tuesday that an oil affiliate had succeeded in striking oil reserves in Papua New Guinea which would yield 2,000 barrels-per-day (bpd).
Mitsubishi Oil said in a statement that a test well called "Moran 1X" was sunk to a depth of 2,940 to 2,976 metres in block PDL-2 and yielded crude oil amounting to 2,000 barrels-per-day (bpd).
The crude is light in quality -- 44 on the American Petroleum Institute measurement -- and similar to Kutubu crude, which is already being produced in block PDL-2, it said.
Potential reserves had yet to be confirmed, but commercial production was expected to start swiftly through the use of existing facilities from the Kutubu project, the statement said.
The Moran 1X test well is about 10 km north of the Agogo field, which produces 100,000 barrels of Kutubu crude daily.
Commercial production of Kutubu crude began in June 1992, and cumulative output reached 170 million barrels in August, the statement said.
The Mitsubishi Oil affiliate, Japan Papua New Guinea Petroleum Co Ltd, has 4.8 percent of the development rights in block PDL-2.

Other shareholders are Chevron Corp with 19.4 percent, British Petroleum Co Plc with 19.4 percent, Ampolex Ltd with 16.5 percent, Broken Hill Proprietary Co Ltd with 9.7 percent, and Oil Search Ltd with 7.8 percent, a Mitsubishi Oil spokesman said.
He said Papua New Guinea owns the remaining 22.5 percent.
